# Releases
## @inngest/ci@0.7.1

### Patch Changes

- [#1833](https://github.com/inngest/inngest-js/pull/1833)
[`e43927da`](https://github.com/inngest/inngest-js/commit/e43927dac0765012d25593579f02cff8fe464bba)
Thanks [@jpwilliams](https://github.com/jpwilliams)! - GitHub checks now
open with the one fact you came for, in a callout: how long a cache hit
saved, which test failed and where, or that a failure is probably
infrastructure and a re-run is the fix. Every link and button sits in
one row, and a running job lists each command once it starts. A failed
job offers "Re-run, no cache", and a job waiting on a build says that it
is not stuck.

  A failed pipeline offers "Re-run all" and "Re-run, no cache".

The pipeline's check shows how far along it is while it runs, and ends
with the time the cache saved, the critical path, the slowest jobs, a
job graph and a timeline. A failed pipeline lists each failed job with
the reason and a link to its check, and a cancelled one says it was
cancelled.

Problems your tools find land as annotations on the lines they are
about: type errors from `tsc --pretty false`, failed,
snapshot-mismatched and flaky tests, and lint from eslint and biome. A
command that writes or prints its report as JSON, such as `vitest run
--reporter=json --outputFile=results.json`, is read on its own, and
`report.results("vitest", "results.json")` reads the file of a tool a
script runs. A rule that repeats on many lines becomes one annotation,
and a check carries at most 200.
## inngest@4.26.2

### Patch Changes

- [#1856](https://github.com/inngest/inngest-js/pull/1856)
[`6193fc27`](https://github.com/inngest/inngest-js/commit/6193fc27bd2b1a6dd865b4ee20be82e7519e1b1b)
Thanks [@jpwilliams](https://github.com/jpwilliams)! - Experimental:
command shims for Sandboxes. `tool.shim()` makes a program on the
command's `PATH` call a handler in your app first. The handler gets the
command's `sandbox`, so it can do privileged work in your app and reply
with the result, run the real program (as called, or with another
`argv`, extra `env` or `stdin`), or refuse. Credentials never need to
enter the sandbox:

  ```ts
  import { tool } from "inngest/experimental";

  await sandbox.$({
    shims: [
      tool.shim("terraform", ({ argv, run, refuse }) => {
        return argv[0] === "apply"
          ? refuse("apply goes through a pull request")
          : run();
      }),
      tool.shim.config({ REGION: "iad" }),
    ],
  }).sh`terraform plan && inngest-tool config REGION`;
  ```

`shims` is accepted by `commands.run()` and `# inngest and takes only
`tool.shim()`values. Code in the sandbox reads settings
with`inngest-tool config NAME`and lists the shims with`inngest-tool
shims`. Commands with tools or shims can now run longer than five
minutes, `exitCodes`works with them, and a timeout fails as
a`sandbox_exec_timed_out`error. Shims use a small static`inngest-tool`
binary that the SDK puts into the sandbox when it is missing.
